title: Rollout tuning postmortem (draft)
body:
Summary:
We observed a steady degradation in panel render latency and analytic pipeline backpressure during the 2027-12-28 UI rollout window. Impact was visible on the canary cohort (5% of traffic) starting 11:15 UTC and widened to ~25% by 12:02 UTC due to an overaggressive traffic ramp. Surface impacts: slow panel loads (200–700ms regression vs baseline), a spike in slow queries to the feature flag service, and backlog growth in the telemetry ingestion Lambda chain causing delayed metrics ingestion.

Primary timeline (quick):
- 10:45 UTC: feature flag rollout triggered (canary 5%) per rollout plan.
- 11:15 UTC: SRE alert — 95th pct panel render latency crossed 450ms for canary.
- 11:25 UTC: Console team triage call, initial suspicion: frontend bundle change.
- 11:35 UTC: Observability shows correlated increase in feature-flag read latency and redis cache miss rate.
- 11:47 UTC: Canary ramp scheduled (to 25%) started by automation; operator ignored early alert.
- 12:02 UTC: Errors in telemetry pipeline increased; ingestion queue lag hit 18 minutes.
- 12:15 UTC: Partial rollback to previous artifact for 25% cohort; canary split reduced.
- 12:40 UTC: Full rollback for canary; metrics begin to recover.
- 13:30 UTC: System returned to baseline.

Root causes (working hypotheses):
1) Client-side: a new client-side metric flusher added synchronous startup work that increased cold render paths for first panel load. Code path serialized a feature-flag check + heavy JSON.parse on a large 12KB blob.
2) Infra/serving: feature flag service saw higher-than-expected QPS due to the new flusher hitting flags on init. This caused cascading cache misses to Redis and increased p99 response times.
3) Rollout process: automation ramp advanced to 25% despite active alerts (no automated rollback). The escalation path for delaying an automated ramp is ambiguous in the runbook.

Supporting telemetry snippets (queries we used):
- Panel render latency: SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 95) FROM panel_load WHERE env = 'canary' AND ts > '2027-12-28T10:00:00Z';
- Feature flag latency by instance: group_by(instance) p50/p95 over 10m windows
- Redis miss ratio: sum(misses)/sum(requests) grouped by cache_key_prefix
- Telemetry ingestion lag: max(message_age_seconds) from telemetry.ingest.queue
(added to linked_artifacts: Linear ticket with query IDs)

Immediate contributing factors observed:
- The new flusher triggered per-panel initialization on navigation (not debounced) causing excess flag reads.
- A recent Redis config change reduced maxclients from 2000 -> 1200 (deployed earlier same week for GC tuning) which lowered headroom.
- Runbook escalation: on-call did not trigger manual hold; the playbook does not clearly mark the automated ramp step as safe-to-run-if-warning.

Mitigations applied during incident:
- 12:15 UTC: Manual throttle via feature-flag rollout controller reduced ramp and prevented further expansion.
- 12:20–12:40 UTC: Reverted frontend artifact for canary cohort (deployed previous stable bundle).
- 12:35 UTC: SRE temporarily increased Redis maxclients and adjusted eviction tuning to clear backlog.
- 12:50 UTC: Telemetry workers scaled up (horizontal autoscale target bumped) to reduce ingestion lag.

Action items (owners and rough ETA):
- Short (1–3 days):
  - Debounce client flag reads on panel init; change flusher to async background fire-and-forget (owner: Priya, ETA: 2028-01-03).
  - Revert or re-audit the large JSON blob schema; split into smaller keys where possible (owner: Diego, ETA: 2028-01-05).
  - Add a pre-ramp gate in the rollout automation that pauses on active alerts matching latency/queue-lag signals (owner: Ethan, ETA: 2028-01-06).
- Mid (1–3 weeks):
  - Restore Redis headroom safely: implement staged validation for GC tuning changes and add capacity runbook (owner: SRE team: Lina, ETA: 2028-01-20).
  - Add synthetic canary tests for feature-flag latency (owner: eng-observability, ETA: 2028-01-18).
- Long (1–3 months):
  - Rework rollout automation to support automatic rollback thresholds for combined metrics (latency + queue lag) and a safer staged ramp algorithm (owner: console-tooling infra, ETA: 2028-03-01).
  - Telemetry pipeline refactor to decouple ingestion from synchronous UI-paths (owner: telemetry infra, ETA: 2028-04-01).

Runbook updates needed:
- Clarify manual hold steps and who may override an automated ramp.
- Add explicit metric thresholds that disable ramps (95th panel latency > 400ms OR ingestion lag > 5 minutes).
- Add a short checklist to verify redis capacity post config changes before any production rollout.

Open questions / follow-ups for postmortem meeting:
- Did the automation properly respect the canary circuit-breaker signals but fail to act because alerts weren't surfaced as inhibiting? (investigate alert-to-gate mapping)
- Should we introduce a short cooldown window between ramps and analytics evaluation windows?
- Is the large client schema necessary, or did a recent telemetry-driven change bloat the payload?

Notes-to-self and sticky operational learnings:
- When telemetry or analytic code touches the render path, treat as high-risk and require explicit perf sign-off.
- Small infra knobs (redis maxclients) can become single points of failure when rollout increases parallelism; better to include safety margins.
- Rollouts are socio-technical: automation + clear human override policy = safer system.

Meeting invite for formal postmortem:
- Invitees: console UI eng, eng-observability, SRE, product owner for rollout, telemetry infra. Proposed slot: 2028-01-06 16:00 UTC (30m).

Draft status: this is a working draft intended for review prior to formal postmortem. Add any missing telemetry queries, logs, and PR references below.

Quick links / references:
- Linear: CON-5123 (feature-flag pressure on rollout)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console-ui/pull/842 (client flusher change)
- Redis config change: infra-ops PR #1295
- Observability dashboards: /dashboards/panel-load-rollout-2027-12-28

Appendix (raw notes from triage call):
- 11:30 — "looks like json.parse on init is the hot path" — Priya
- 11:37 — "redis miss spikes line up with slow renders, but need to confirm causation" — Lina
- 11:50 — "automation ramped; we need to pause ramping when alerts fire" — Marion
- To-do in-call: gate automation -> Ethan, debounce client -> Priya, rollback artifact -> Diego

Please add any additional observations, repro steps, or log snippets here. Will convert to formal postmortem after triage review and attach timeline logs and graphs.
